details.description: gpt-4-1106-preview is the first GPT-4 Turbo preview snapshot, announced at OpenAI's DevDay in November 2023. It introduced a 128K-token context window (expanded from GPT-4's original 8K), a JSON mode for structurally valid output, parallel function calling, and a seed parameter for more reproducible outputs; OpenAI described its knowledge of world events as current to April 2023. OpenAI's deprecations page currently schedules this snapshot for shutdown on October 23, 2026, recommending gpt-5.6-sol as the replacement (a since-superseded September 2025 notice had set an earlier March 26, 2026 date); Azure's current GPT-4 documentation already treats the GA gpt-4 (turbo-2024-04-09) release as the replacement for all 2023-era GPT-4 preview snapshots, including this one.
advantages: Introduced JSON mode, giving structurally valid output for data pipelines where earlier GPT-4 versions could produce parsing failures.
Expanded the context window from GPT-4's original 8K tokens to 128K tokens at launch.
Added a seed parameter for more reproducible, deterministic outputs, alongside parallel function calling.
disadvantages: Scheduled for shutdown by OpenAI on October 23, 2026, per OpenAI's deprecations page, which recommends gpt-5.6-sol as the replacement.
Azure's current GPT-4 documentation lists the GA gpt-4 (turbo-2024-04-09) release as the replacement for all previous GPT-4 preview models, including this one.
OpenAI's own November 2023 announcement described this model's knowledge of world events as current only to April 2023.
use_cases: Chat and text-generation tasks requiring a 128K-token context window
Applications needing reproducible outputs via the seed parameter, e.g. regression testing

notes: Catalog's deprecation_date of 2026-10-23 for this target matches OpenAI's own deprecations page: a 2026-04-22 dated entry lists gpt-4-1106-preview's shutdown as October 23, 2026 (replacement gpt-5.6-sol). That entry supersedes an earlier 2025-09-26 dated entry on the same page, which had set a March 26, 2026 shutdown (replacement 'gpt-5 or gpt-4.1'); the page keeps both as a changelog, newest first, so October 23, 2026 is the current figure and it agrees with the catalog -- no mismatch remains. Grouped azure/openai URIs both refer to the same OpenAI-authored 1106 preview snapshot, so treated as one model. Could not reach openai.com's original November 2023 DevDay post directly (403 on fetch); its 'knowledge to April 2023' line is corroborated via a quote reproduced in the linked OpenAI community-forum thread.
